intended_object: The q-integer (q-analogue of n), [n]_q = 1 + q + ⋯ + q^{n-1}, evaluated at a natural number q. Inferred from the docstring and from its use: the library counts complete flags in vector spaces over finite fields 𝔽_q via the q-factorial ∏[i]_q.
explanation:
The body is `∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, q ^ i`, which is exactly 1 + q + ⋯ + q^{n-1}. It gives the right values at the edge cases: [0]_q = 0 (empty sum) and [1]_q = 1, and both are proved as lemmas in the file. Mathlib has no definition of q-integers. It has only general geometric-sum lemmas such as `geom_sum_mul_of_one_le`, which the library uses to prove [n]_q·(q−1) = q^n − 1.

The same formula would make sense in any semiring, and the q-integer is also often treated as a polynomial in q. But here it is used to count combinatorial objects: [n]_q is the number of points of a projective space over 𝔽_q, and the q-factorial is the number of complete flags. Natural-number values are the natural setting for that. The module documentation also states explicitly that q is a natural number, and the library separately introduces a polynomial version for its asymptotic analysis. So the restriction to ℕ is not an unwarranted narrowing, and the definition is faithful.
